title: The 10 Best Cordless Reciprocating Saws
subtitle: Battery-powered demo saws ranked from live Amazon data — cut, prune, and tear out anywhere.
intro: A reciprocating saw (the tool everyone calls a Sawzall) pushes a long blade back and forth to rip through wood, metal, nail-embedded lumber, PVC, and tree branches. It's the demolition and rough-cut workhorse. Cordless models let you use it up a ladder, in a crawlspace, or out in the yard with no cord. Most of the best sell as a bare tool, so check whether a pick is a bare tool or a ready-to-use kit, and which battery platform it rides. Need maximum sustained power for the least money? See the corded list.

products.name: DEWALT DCS380B 20V MAX Reciprocating Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: Amazon's #1 seller in power reciprocating saws: DEWALT's standard 20V MAX recip with a 1-1/8 in stroke, a 4-position blade clamp, and a 3-year warranty, at $129 sold by Amazon. It's a bare tool, so it makes the most sense if you already own a DEWALT 20V MAX battery.
products.best_for: DEWALT 20V MAX owners who want a full-size demo and pruning saw.
products.skip_if: You own no DEWALT batteries; it ships without a battery or charger.
pros: 1-1/8 in stroke, longer than the compact saws here
4-position blade clamp for flush cuts, tool-free blade change
cons: Tool only: no battery or charger
The listing doesn't claim a brushless motor in its title or feature list

products.name: RYOBI ONE+ 18V Cordless Reciprocating Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: The pick if you're already on RYOBI ONE+. A 3,400-SPM saw with a 1-inch stroke and tool-free blade change, sold as a bare tool. Add a ONE+ battery and go.
products.best_for: RYOBI ONE+ owners who want the fastest stroke rate here.
products.skip_if: You want to buy from Amazon with a full warranty; it's a third-party listing.
pros: Fastest stroke rate here at 3,400 SPM
cons: Tool only — no battery or charger
Not brushless
Amazon listing is a third-party seller with a 30-day warranty; check the price elsewhere too

products.name: DEWALT DCS367B 20V MAX XR Brushless Reciprocating Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: The best cordless recip money can buy — brushless, compact, and brutally capable, with 10,800 reviews at 4.8 stars. A 1-1/8" stroke rips through nail-embedded lumber like a corded saw. Bare tool.
products.best_for: Remodelers on DEWALT 20V MAX who cut nail-embedded lumber regularly.
products.skip_if: You prune a few branches a year; it's near $180 bare.
cons: Near $180 for a bare tool
Overkill for occasional pruning

products.name: DEWALT DCS387B 20V MAX Compact Reciprocating Saw (tool only)
products.verdict: The compact DEWALT that fits between studs and into tight spots, with a full 1-1/8" stroke and 4,500 reviews at 4.8 stars. Cheaper than the brushless XR if you don't need the last bit of runtime.
products.best_for: Tight spots between studs on DEWALT 20V MAX, for less than the brushless model.
cons: Tool only — no battery or charger

products.verdict: The pro's SAWZALL — Milwaukee invented the reciprocating saw, and the M18 FUEL is a brushless demolition monster with a huge 1-1/4" stroke. The pick if you're on the M18 platform.
products.best_for: Milwaukee M18 owners doing heavy demolition with a long 1-1/4 in stroke.

cons: Tool only — no battery or charger
Second-priciest saw here, behind the DEWALT DCS367B

products.name: Milwaukee 2719-20 M18 FUEL HACKZALL (tool only)

products.best_for: Milwaukee M18 owners who want a one-handed saw for tight spots and overhead cuts.
products.skip_if: You want a full-size demo saw or don't own M18 batteries.
pros: One-handed design, 1.8 kg per the listing
cons: Tool only: no battery or charger

avoid.name: Olmlmo 21V Brushless Cordless Reciprocating Saw Kit with 2 x 4.0Ah Batteries and 8 Blades (RS03)
avoid.flag: Listing contradicts itself on power, weight and blades
avoid.verdict: A cheap kit whose own listing can't agree on what you're buying: the bullets and the spec table give different wattage, weight and blade material. Buy a saw whose specs you can trust.
reasons: Power: the bullets claim a 500W brushless motor; the spec table says 200 watts.
Weight: the bullets say it weighs only 3 lbs; the spec table lists 7.59 pounds.
Blades: the kit list says 8 carbide saw blades, but the spec table gives the blade material as aluminum oxide, which is an abrasive, not a saw-blade material.
Speed is quoted as 3,200 rpm, a rotary-tool unit; reciprocating saws are rated in strokes per minute, so it can't be compared with the saws above.
The RYOBI PCL515B and BLACK+DECKER BDCR20B above are bare tools, but their listings agree with themselves, and both run on battery platforms with large tool lineups.

buyers_guide.a: It pushes a blade back and forth to make fast, rough cuts through almost anything — wood, metal, PVC, drywall, and nail-embedded lumber — plus pruning branches. It's the demolition and remodeling saw; not for fine, straight cuts (that's a circular saw).

A bare tool ships with no battery or charger — great if you own the brand's packs, useless out of the box if you don't. A kit includes a battery, charger, and often blades. Each pick above says which.

Yes. A longer stroke (around 1-1/8 to 1-1/4 inch) uses more of the blade and cuts faster and more aggressively — better for demolition. Shorter strokes (7/8 inch) are gentler and easier one-handed, fine for pruning and light cuts.
Brushless motors run cooler, last longer, and hold power under load — worth it for heavy demolition. For occasional pruning and the odd cut, a brushed saw like the BLACK+DECKER BDCR20B is plenty.
Buy on the same platform as tools you already own (DEWALT 20V MAX, Milwaukee M18, RYOBI ONE+, CRAFTSMAN V20). If you own nothing yet, a self-contained kit like the SEESII avoids the platform lock-in.
